claim_grade: Source tier: Tier 1 (World Bank institution; sources/audit/people-tiers.json lists 'World Bank' in tier-1 and a 'World Bank country diagnostics' entry: statutory facts A, coverage figures B, recommendations C; cite the institution first). Grades: report's descriptions of Korean statutes, agency roles, dates and procedures = A/B (A where a statute/act is named, B where a figure comes from a Korean ministry); 15-30 per cent pre-1989 figure = B (secondary, see uncertainties); 2020 AMVRs = B (MOLIT figures); 'Lessons Learned' (PDF pp.9-10, 40-44) and the Jobs Agenda/growth claims (PDF p.10) = C (authors' judgement), not support for causal claims; claims about collateral/credit access and infrastructure investment are D (asserted, no evidence given). The report is descriptive; no Georgist/LVT framing, no author Tier-2 issue.

content_summary.pre_1989_fragmentation: Four agencies, four values (PDF p.15, printed 5): Taxable Standard Market Value (Ministry of Home Affairs, local tax), Reference Market Value (NTS, national tax, only designated speculative areas, fixed multiplier on land grade), National Land Value (Ministry of Construction, compensation), Appraised Market Value (Korea Appraisal Board). Quote: 'consistently lagged actual market prices, typically at only 15-30 percent of prevailing transaction values' (p.15, applies to the Taxable Standard Market Value ONLY). Exec Summary (PDF p.6) and Intro (p.11-12) generalise to all four ('at most 15 to 30 percent'); Annex 4 (PDF p.50, from Maeil Business Newspaper 1998, p.3, four parcels, index 100 = appraiser value) shows Taxable Standard Market Value at 18.2, 23.0, 18.3, 4.9 per cent and Reference Market Value at 65.4, 74.6, 89.9, 40.6 per cent. Annex 3 (PDF p.49, source Chae 1992): National Land Value covered 334,000 parcels 1973-87; Taxable Standard representative land about 1% of taxable parcels (41,818 in 1984), index-table area 121,211 in 1988. Causes given: no clear standards, irregular surveys, subjective decisions of untrained officials (p.15). Consequences: local governments underfunded, contested compensation, no penalty on speculative holding (PDF p.6, 12). The 15-30% figure is the report's own statement; it is not attributed in text to a named source (Annex 3-4 sources are Chae 1992 and Maeil 1998).
content_summary.1989_act_and_1991: Public Notice of Values and Appraisal of Lands, etc. Act enacted 1 April 1989 (Annex 12, PDF p.65) 'based on a comprehensive national land survey and the philosophy of the public concept of land ownership' (p.16); unified survey schedules, standards and responsible agencies; annual standardized survey and announcement; unified land appraiser and authorised appraiser into 'certified appraiser'. 1991: nationwide rollout of publicly announced (individual) land values, 'more than 30 million parcels at that time' (PDF p.13, printed 3); Annex 12 says the 1995 amendment gave the legal basis for individual publicly announced land prices. 2005: Act on Public Announcement of Real Estate Values and Appraisal (houses added); 2016 full revision splits it into the Act on the Public Announcement of Real Estate Values and the Act on Appraisal and Appraisers; 2016 partial 'single appraisal' for representative parcels and delegation of calculation/verification to REB; April 2020 amendment set target ratios for market-price reflection (PDF p.65-66).
content_summary.mass_valuation_design: National government selects 600,000 representative (standard) parcels from roughly 35 million total (PDF p.17, printed 7; p.23); base date January 1 each year; representative values published 37 times and individual values 36 times to date (p.17). Representative parcels: surveyed and valued by certified appraisers (appraisal corporations) selected under REB-set standards, with REB managing and checking (p.20; Annex 1 p.46: hearings with landowners, consultation with local heads, Land Valuation Committee deliberation). REB does not itself appraise land; for houses REB appraises representative houses directly (p.20). Index table: built by REB per smallest admin unit (eup/myeon/dong) per zoning type via a hedonic price model; footnote 30 (PDF p.27) says it is a multiple linear regression whose coefficients become the index ratios; worked example Figure 3 (p.26): representative 13,900,000 KRW/m2 x terrain ratio 1.16 = 16,124,000; mild slope vs flat = 1.16. Individual parcels: local governments (si/gun/gu) survey characteristics (Table 2, p.27) and apply index ratios in KOREPS; heads of local government determine and announce; verification by appraisal corporations (land) or REB (houses); mandatory public inspection; objection within 30 days, local government to respond within 30 days of the deadline (p.27). Appraiser numbers: 4,877 certified appraisers in 2025 (p.21), profession-wide; the report gives NO figure for how many appraise the 600,000 representative parcels. REB has 30 branch offices (p.20). Houses: same three-step design since 2005 (apartments 2005, all houses 2006, fn 13 p.18; non-residential not announced); Annex 15 (pp.69-72) gives land and building index tables separately for detached houses; valuation approaches: sales comparison mandatory, income approach selective, cost approach rarely (p.71).
content_summary.administrative_uses: 'some 60' functions (PDF p.6, 11, 17, 19, 40). Annex 7 (PDF pp.53-58) tabulates them: Welfare 10, Charges 4, Administrative 19, Taxation 8, Real-estate appraisal etc. 19 = 60. Welfare: basic pension and disability pension (assessed value x 0.04 = recognised income), National Basic Livelihood Security, regional health-insurance premiums (property component, indirect), student-loan and scholarship brackets, EITC cut-off (KRW 200m), public rental eligibility, military-service exemption. Charges: development charge (Act on Restitution of Development Gains, Art.10, based on publicly announced land value), reconstruction excess-gains levy (~50% rate), farmland preservation charge, greenbelt charge. Taxation: property tax, acquisition tax (official value as floor), CREHT (threshold KRW 600m, 900m single house), capital gains tax (fallback), inheritance and gift tax, registration and licence tax. Compensation appraisal uses appraisal 'based on representative land' (p.57).
content_summary.digital_systems: 1990 300,000-parcel Representative Land Price DB; ALPA developed 1993, nationwide 1996 (PDF p.23, 18); HPAS for houses; PBLIS 1996; LMIS 1997; KLIS merged LMIS+PBLIS (valuation function moved to KLIS 2005 per p.18 and p.23, but 2003 per Annex 14 p.68 and Annex 17 p.78, and 'KLIS to KRAS 2006' in Annex 17); KRAS 2015 (p.18; Annex 13 says 2014/2015, 18 ledger types; Annex 16 p.73: 37 million parcels and 7 million buildings); KOREPS developed by REB, fully operational January 2024, centralized on G-Cloud (p.23). The report's own dates are inconsistent across main text and annexes; the main-text dates match the scanner.
content_summary.2006_transaction_reporting: Mandatory reporting of actual price within 30 days of contract by buyers, sellers, agents (Annex 1, PDF p.47), effective 1 Jan 2006, to stop 'dual contracts' (under-reporting); verified by RTMS with statistical screening plus expert review (PDF p.42-43). Real Name registration Act 1995 (Annex 17 p.75).
content_summary.revenue_shares_2023: Table 9 (PDF p.36), source Local Tax Statistics Yearbook, Ministry of the Interior and Safety: local consumption 21.9, acquisition 21.6, local income 20.4, property 13.2, automobile 6.5 per cent etc. BUT p.31 (printed 21) says acquisition tax was 16.1 per cent (about USD 13.9bn) and property tax 13.2 per cent (about USD 11.4bn), Ministry of the Interior and Safety 2024; Figure 5 (p.37) labels 2023 as roughly 22 / 13. Exec Summary (p.8) and Conclusion (p.10): 'Property-related taxes account for nearly 30 percent of local government tax income'; this is property tax plus acquisition (and 13.2+16.1=29.3), not property tax alone. Seoul 34.3% and Gyeonggi 26.5% of national property tax revenue (fn 37, p.38). CREHT: total revenue USD 2.94bn (about KRW 4.2tn) in 2023, citing KDI Economic Education 2024 (fn 32, p.28); 'the entire CREHT revenue is redistributed to local governments' with priority to fiscally weaker ones (p.28), via the Local Share Tax Act (1961) and the Real Estate Special Local Share Tax (2005) (Box 1, p.35). Mentions 66% fall in CREHT payers in 2023 only in the KDI reference title (p.45).
content_summary.assessment_to_market_ratios: Quote: 'AMVRs in 2020 were approximately 69.0 percent for multi-unit housing (including apartments), 53.6 percent for single-family houses, and 65.5 percent for land' (PDF p.34, printed 24), attributed to MOLIT; the report says these are 'the baseline levels used in the original 2020 plan, not the latest AMVRs'. 2020 Real Estate Value Realization Plan targeted 90 per cent (land 2028, apartments 2030, single-family 2035) then revised (p.33); 2023 reverted to 2020 levels with reduced FMVRs, official multi-unit values fell 18.6% and property tax revenue 13.4% (p.39); 2026 multi-unit AMVR held at 69%. Tax base = official value x Fair Market Value Ratio (FMVR): residential 60 per cent (43-45 per cent single-home households 2026), land and non-residential buildings 70 per cent; statutory range 40-80% (30-70% single-home) set by Presidential Decree; local rate discretion +/-50% (pp.30, 33-35). Political resistance: the report says only that CREHT's reach into single-home households 'sparked public and political debate' (p.28) and that government revised the plan 'in response to concerns over tax burdens' (p.39); no named opponents, no detail.
content_summary.land_vs_building: Korea publishes a per-parcel land value (publicly announced individual land value, the 공시지가 of wiki South Korea page, per m2) for every parcel since 1989/1991. Since 2005 residential property tax uses combined land+building 'single taxable unit' (PDF p.7, 13, 38). Non-residential buildings: 'assessed by appraising the values of building structures and underlying land separately' (p.30). Land is taxed in its own three categories under Local Tax Act Art.106/112: comprehensively aggregated (idle/non-business) 0.2-0.5%, separately aggregated (business) 0.2-0.4%, separately taxed (farm/forest 0.07%, factory 0.2%, golf/high-end 0.4%) (pp.31-33); buildings 0.25% commercial, 0.5% industrial, 12.5% congestion-zone factories, 4% luxury (p.36). The report does NOT say whether land values are as-if-vacant and does not use the terms site value, land value tax or Georgism; land-value characteristics include actual land use (Table 2). Prior to the 2005 reform the report says 'valuing land and buildings separately' showed limits as housing prices rose (p.7).
content_summary.public_concept_of_land_laws: Annex 6 (PDF p.52): Public Concept of Land Ownership defined as 'Land is a shared asset of the state or society as a whole. Private ownership is recognized, but restrictions on use and disposition may be imposed to prioritize the public interest.' Enacted 1989 (not 1990): Act on Ceiling on Residential Land Ownership (repealed 1998); Land Excess Profit Tax Act (progressive tax on land holdings above a threshold; repealed 1998); Development Gain Reclamation (Restitution) Act (reclaims part of development gains; amended 2023, still in force). Constitutional Court: 'In 1994 ... ruled the Land Excess Profit Tax Act (1989) unconstitutional due to excessive burden, double taxation, and irrational tax rates', while upholding the Public Concept of Land Ownership (p.52). Nothing on the Court's treatment of the Ceiling Act or of the Comprehensive Land Tax. Footnotes 1-2 (p.15): the 'Excess Land Gains Tax' (anti-idle-land tax on gains above the normal rate) and the 'Comprehensive Land Tax' (progressive tax on aggregate national landholding per owner) are both 'abolished'; no dates or reasons given, and the report's names differ from Annex 6's ('Land Excess Profit Tax'); Annex 5 (p.51) separately lists a 'Land Value Increment Tax Law' and 'Comprehensive Land Tax Law' in 1989. CREHT (2005) replaced the local Comprehensive Land Tax with a national progressive tax, individual basis then household basis from 2006 (Annex 1, p.47). Greenbelt 1971, Land Transaction Permission 1978, Housing Site Ownership Ceiling 1989 (p.13).
content_summary.third_party_figures_to_attribute: MOLIT: 2020 AMVRs, valuation procedures (MOLIT 2023, 2024, 2025a/b); Ministry of the Interior and Safety (Local Tax Statistics Yearbook 2024): 2023 local-tax shares, 13.2/16.1(21.6)%, regional property-tax revenue; KDI Economic Education 2024: CREHT revenue USD 2.94bn, 2023; Chae 1992 (Korea Research Institute for Human Settlements): pre-1989 parcel counts, Annex 3; Maeil Business Newspaper 8 June 1998: Annex 4 price discrepancies; Hong and Hwang 2024 (Korea Research Institute for Local Administration): 2019 and 2021 CREHT rate rises 'contributed to reductions in housing price disparities and asset inequality' (p.28; secondary, one study); OECD Economic Surveys: Korea 2024: that Korea's progressive national property taxation balances redistribution with fiscal sustainability (p.28; secondary). Report refers to 'World Bank 2023, Korea: Land and Property Valuation Case Study' (p.45) as an unseen precursor. Statutory thresholds in Annex 7 (CREHT KRW 600m / 900m single house) appear to be older than the 1.2bn/1.4bn figures in the wiki's 2026 Korea Herald items: do not use the Annex 7 CREHT threshold without checking.
content_summary.lessons_C_grade: Four lessons (PDF pp.9-10, 40-44): (1) legal split of government-produced public values from private appraisals, a central authority with mandate, continuous professional capacity; (2) connected data systems, common standards, phased pilots; (3) standardized spatial data and mandatory verified transaction reporting; (4) keep valuation separate from tax-rate decisions, using an administrative adjustment ratio (FMVR) with statutory floors and ceilings, and accessible 30-day objections. All are authors' judgement (C). The report says 'Korea's experience is not a blueprint' (p.9). Growth/jobs/collateral/credit claims (p.10) are asserted without evidence (D).

existing_wiki_coverage: Corpus digest grep (Korea, Seoul, CREHT, comprehensive real estate, official land price, 공시지가, jongbusae) finds only places/south-korea (stub: false, last_reviewed 2026-08-16; excerpt about KLC/LH public development) and concepts/credit-window-guidance (unrelated) plus research/mohamed-south-africa (unrelated 'Korea' contrast); no research page, objection or concept page covers Korea's valuation system. places/south-korea.md currently has: Overview (KLC/LH, Ryan-Collins et al.), The Public Development Model (land readjustment, Seoul Solution), Significance (says only that Korea 'also has recurring property and (at various points) capital-gains-style land taxes' and that the page 'does not yet assess that literature'), Contemporary Georgist Politics (Lee Jae-myung land dividend; Budget Office dual-tax comparison, rates 'local property tax (progressive rates 0.05-0.4%)' and jongbusae 0.5-5.0%; August 2026 jongbusae overhaul, exemption 1.2bn to 1.4bn won), and Georgist Civil Society (Landforall.kr map of 공시지가 per Doucet, Land+Freedom Institute). The page mentions 공시지가 only via Landforall.kr; it has no description of how official values are produced, no CREHT redistribution, no history of the 1989 laws. Source 6 (Doucet, 'How to Value Land: Korean style!') is Tier 2 advocacy; the WB report is a Tier 1 primary-institution description of the same system and can now carry the factual weight. concepts/mass-appraisal-methods.md has an 'Existing Practice at Scale' list (Estonia, Denmark, Australian states, US) with no Korea; its ratio-study section has no national-scale level-of-assessment case. objections/land-cannot-be-assessed.md has points 1 through 5 (with 3a-3g) and no Korea; point 1 says 'It is already done at scale' with Estonia, Denmark, Australia, US only. concepts/site-value.md and research/gloudemans-lvt-assessment-feasibility.md have no Korea mention. Research-page precedents: research/world-bank-property-tax-determinants.md (authors [World Bank], year 2020, tier important, subcategory wiki-research-inequality, source_url on documents1.worldbank.org) and research/imf-taxing-immovable-property.md (same pattern). Pakistan has a World Bank diagnostic cited from places/pakistan without a research page.

proposed_enrichments.anchor_sentence: - Most US assessments already publish a land/improvement split, though the quality and methodology of that split varies widely across jurisdictions.[4]
proposed_enrichments.what_is_new: A national-scale representative-parcel plus hedonic index-table CAMA system valuing roughly 35 million land parcels annually, with the 'representative' appraisals done by certified private appraisers and the index tables by a national board; level-of-assessment of 53.6 to 69 per cent (2020, MOLIT) shows level was a policy choice separate from model accuracy. State plainly it values parcels (not as-if-vacant) and that houses are taxed as land plus building combined, so it is evidence for scale and design, not for land/building separation. Optional second sentence in the ratio-studies section after '...not a Georgist-specific workaround.[14]' on the Korean AMVR as a level (not uniformity) measure; only if the writer wants it.

proposed_enrichments.anchor_sentence: a caution that outsourcing assessment to the private sector is not a reliable shortcut around administrative-capacity constraints.
proposed_enrichments.what_is_new: Korea as a national-scale existence proof of parcel-level mass valuation built from a sample of benchmarks, with a public legal separation of government values from private appraisals and an annual cycle; the report's own lessons say technology without data/governance fails (C). Hedge: it shows annual national valuation of land parcels is administratively feasible, not that land can be separated from buildings.

new_page_warranted: Yes. Slug suggestion research/world-bank-korea-land-property-valuation. Reasons: Tier 1 institutional primary description of a national mass-valuation system in 80 pages with detailed A/B facts that no existing page holds; follows the world-bank-property-tax-determinants and imf-taxing-immovable-property precedents; gives the Korea place page a citable Tier 1 source instead of relying on Tier 2 advocacy commentary (Doucet) for Korean valuation. Sections: Summary, What the Report Covers, How Official Values Are Produced, Uses and Taxes, Reform Lessons (C-labelled), Limits (not an LVT study; no vacant-land basis; internal inconsistencies), Bears On (land-cannot-be-assessed, South Korea). Sources entry should read impersonally, e.g. 'World Bank Group, Urban, Resilience and Land Korea Team (2026), Unlocking Value ..., 80 pp.; read in full; descriptions of Korean law and administration B, authors' lessons C; figures from MOLIT, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and KDI are attributed to those bodies' sources via the report' (grade codes and access notes live in Sources only, per EDITORIAL 4b).
scanner_premises_checked: CONFIRMED: title, WB authorship (URL Korea Team), October 2026 (PDF created 28 Oct 2026), direct PDF served openly; 1989 Act, 1991 rollout, 600,000/35 million, annual update, index tables and hedonic models, about 60 uses, 'Recognized Income', separation of public and private values, ALPA 1993/KLIS 2005/KRAS 2015/KOREPS Jan 2024, 2005 house value system, 2006 reporting, 2020 ratios 69.0/53.6/65.5.

IMPRECISE: 'four fragmented agency valuations (previously capturing only 15-30 percent of market prices)'. The 15-30% applies to the Taxable Standard Market Value; Exec Summary overgeneralises it to all four; the report's own Annex 4 sample shows the NTS Reference Market Value at 41-90% and the National Land Value and Appraised Market Value as the 100 baseline. No named source for 15-30% in the text.

IMPRECISE/INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: 'property taxes about 30 percent of local tax revenue (2023: about 11.4 billion USD property tax at 13.2 percent and 13.9 billion USD acquisition taxes at 16.1 percent)'. Property tax alone is 13.2%; the 'nearly 30 percent' is property plus acquisition tax; and Table 9 (p.36) and the text (p.36) give acquisition tax 21.6% (sum 34.8%), contradicting the 16.1% on p.31. Do not state one figure without saying which; prefer 13.2% property tax (consistent across p.31, p.36, Table 9) and report acquisition as 16.1% or 21.6% with the discrepancy noted in the Sources entry.

MISDATED: 'the 1990 public concept of land laws': the report dates them 1989 (Annex 6). 'Their fate at the Constitutional Court': the report records only the 1994 ruling against the Land Excess Profit Tax Act (and that the Court upheld the Public Concept of Land Ownership); the Ceiling Act and Land Excess Profit Tax were repealed in 1998; the Development Gain Restitution Act survives (amended 2023); the Comprehensive Land Tax and Excess Land Gains Tax are called 'abolished' with no dates; nothing on Court rulings for those. Any Court detail beyond Annex 6 would be outside this source (my recollection that the Court also ruled against the Ceiling Act and the Comprehensive Land Tax is unverified here; do not use).

UNSUPPORTED: 'political resistance to raising [ratios]': the report supports a mild form (policy walked back in 2023 'in response to concerns over tax burdens'; debate over CREHT reaching single-home owners) but names no actors, votes or events.
UNSUPPORTED: how many appraisers: only the profession total (4,877, 2025) is given; no count for the representative-parcel survey.

UNSUPPORTED by this source: the scanner's 'Development Discourse' provenance and 'Verified absent' lines (not checkable from the report); 'complements the Doucet piece' (the report does not cite Doucet or Landforall).

NOT IN REPORT: any Georgist/LVT framing, a land-only (site) value taxation system, Henry George; 'land value as distinct from building value' is answered only as: land parcels are valued individually; houses are valued as land+building since 2005; non-residential assessed separately; land taxed in its own rate categories.
uncertainties: 1) The landing page's download button could not be read (JS-rendered), so the PDF URL is the scanner's, accepted because it served the PDF openly with matching title/content; no other source was consulted. 2) Report has internal inconsistencies: acquisition tax share 16.1% vs 21.6%; KLIS 2005 vs 2003/2006 and KRAS 2014 vs 2015; Annex 12 says the 2016 Act introduced a non-residential announcement system while the text says non-residential values are not announced; Exec Summary overgeneralisation of 15-30%; Annex 17 calls the repealed tax 'Land Excess Profit Tax' but fn 1 'Excess Land Gains Tax'. 3) CREHT thresholds in Annex 7 look stale against the wiki's Korea Herald figures; no CREHT rates are given. 4) Whether Korean official land values are as-if-vacant is not stated. 5) 'Some 60' functions is given as a count and reconciles with Annex 7 (10+4+19+8+19). 6) Pre-1989 and Annex 3-4 data come from secondary Korean sources (Chae 1992; a 1998 newspaper). 7) Authors' growth/credit claims and Jobs Agenda framing are advocacy-style institutional claims, not evidence. 8) Report is dated October 2026 and describes 2026 policy (FMVR 43-45% for 2026); recent facts may change. 9) Quotations to use (all under 50 words): 'consistently lagged actual market prices, typically at only 15-30 percent of prevailing transaction values' (PDF p.15, printed 5); 'Land is a shared asset of the state or society as a whole. Private ownership is recognized, but restrictions on use and disposition may be imposed to prioritize the public interest.' (PDF p.52, printed 42); 'In 1994, the Constitutional Court ruled the Land Excess Profit Tax Act (1989) unconstitutional due to excessive burden, double taxation, and irrational tax rates.' (PDF p.52); 'the entire CREHT revenue is redistributed to local governments through intergovernmental transfers designed to promote regional fiscal equalization' (PDF p.28 text, printed 18); 'The national government selects 600,000 standard parcels deemed representative from among the nation's roughly 35 million total parcels' (PDF p.17, printed 7).
